roadmap.summary: Chambers is a genuinely deep 32-room legal practice platform: encryption-per-matter, ethical walls, audit logging, honest "no fabrication" discipline, and several real end-to-end gates (Research→Citation Check→Brief Writer→Filing) are all built and green on the harness. The dominant failure mode is not missing rooms but promised controls that don't actually bind: the Conflicts "gate" enforces nothing, the limitation clock is computed off the wrong cause of action and rolled forward past a Saturday into a false-safe date, and the Citation Check certificate can be printed over text edited after verification. Highest leverage now is hardening the malpractice-critical seams already half-built — make the conflicts gate block intake/retainer, fix limitation date math, and close the verify→edit→certify loophole — because they are low-to-medium effort and each removes a way the tool can be quietly, dangerously wrong. After that, the biggest new-build value is closing the loops the connectors already reach (automated citation resolution via the CanLII/CourtListener code sitting unwired next door) and the revenue/production deliverables (document production+load files, billing run, trust By-Law 9) that keep work and money from staying trapped inside Chambers.

improve_slate.item: Make Room 02 an enforced gate, not an advisory checklist: block Intake's accept path from minting a matter/DEK and block Retainer draft/sign unless a conflictRun exists with outcome 'clear' or 'waiver'.
improve_slate.why: The room is named a Gate and the whole promise is 'no one bills an hour before it clears', but as built a busy lawyer can open a matter and sign a retainer with a pending or declined conflict — the malpractice control does not actually bind.

improve_slate.item: Stop compute() from rolling limitation periods forward to the next business day; weekend/holiday roll-forward must apply to procedural deadlines only, never to on/bc/ab/qc/ny statutory limitations.
improve_slate.why: A limitation that expires on a Saturday is NOT extended to Monday — the claim is statute-barred; the current unconditional roll calendars a false, later 'safe' date on the single most malpractice-critical deadline in the file. Tiny fix, catastrophic if wrong.

improve_slate.item: Key Intake's limitation lookup to the claim type it collected instead of rulesFor(jur).find(id.includes('limitation')), and handle jurisdictions (us-fed) with no limitation rule instead of silently leaving the clock null.
improve_slate.why: In NY a contract claim silently gets the 3yr PI rule (should be 6yr CPLR 213(2)) and us-fed produces no clock at all, yet the file still reads 'screened' — a litigator relies on a date keyed to the wrong cause of action.

improve_slate.item: Close the verify→edit→certify loophole: invalidate verified citation_instances (or block the certificate) when a draft's updatedAt is later than scannedAt, so an edit in Brief Writer after a clean scan cannot still print a 'clear' certificate.
improve_slate.why: The certificate is the exact artifact a lawyer hands a court under Ko v. Li / the Federal Court AI notice; certifying authorities for text that changed since verification is the precise failure this room exists to prevent.

improve_slate.item: Make Brief Writer's 'Send to Citation Check' actually extract and mint citation_instances (or queue extraction) instead of only flipping status to 'cite-check' while flashing that room 08 queued them.
improve_slate.why: The sellable feature is the brief→cite-check→file gate; the lawyer trusts citations are queued when nothing was, and discovers an empty table of authorities at the worst moment.

improve_slate.item: Wire retainer signing into the money side: on status 'signed', post the fee/trust-replenishment expectation to Trust & Books and notify it, instead of writing only a date.
improve_slate.why: The spec promises executed retainers 'become live commitments in Trust & Books the moment they're executed'; without the link the firm has a signed fee agreement the money side of the platform knows nothing about.

improve_slate.item: Add a document-view route in Document Review so a reviewer can read a document's full decrypted text; today blobs decrypt only to build a 45-char search snippet.
improve_slate.why: Coding privilege/responsiveness on a title and a fragment is how privileged material gets produced and responsive material gets missed — a review tool you cannot read documents in is not a review tool.

improve_slate.item: When governing jurisdiction changes in Jurisdiction Desk, list/flag/route the now-stale computed deadlines (esp. the limitation bar) for recompute instead of leaving a prose caveat that they aren't retroactively recalculated.
improve_slate.why: A jurisdiction change (ON↔NY, 2yr vs 3yr) is precisely when limitation math breaks; a note is not a control over the most malpractice-prone date in the file.

improve_slate.item: Give the privilege log real per-document descriptors — author, recipients, date created, and a description of the withheld subject — rather than mapping every entry to 'Solicitor-client privilege'.
improve_slate.why: A log without author/recipient/description is facially deficient under Ontario Schedule B and US Rule 26(b)(5); opposing counsel and the court cannot test the claim, inviting a motion to compel or a waiver finding.

improve_slate.item: Extend Citation Check extraction to statute/section patterns (Limitations Act, 2002, s.4; FRCP 12(a)) and add a manual 'add a cite the extractor missed' row.
improve_slate.why: Statutory miscites currently pass the gate untouched and the 'table of authorities verified' silently omits a whole class of citations while looking complete.

improve_slate.item: Link Evidence Room exhibits to the Document Review Bates/blob they actually are, so P-3/D-1 points at the produced document instead of being retyped by hand; also require a foundation + sponsoring witness before an exhibit can reach 'admitted'.
improve_slate.why: A trial exhibit IS a produced document; retyping it breaks the chain from the Bates-stamped record and creates two sources of truth that drift, and free-text foundation lets an exhibit reach 'admitted' empty.

improve_slate.item: Build the Trial Calendar's headline 'computed back from the trial date' cascade: back-calculate expert disclosure/discovery close/dispositive-motion/pretrial dates and recalculate the chain when the trial date or a trigger moves, instead of independent fixed forward offsets.
improve_slate.why: Back-from-trial computation with automatic recalculation is exactly what a trial lawyer buys a rules engine to do, and it is the room's advertised feature that is entirely unbuilt.

missing_slate.item: Automated citation resolution: call the already-built CanLII API (room 29) and CourtListener/uscourts connectors from inside the Citation Check gate so a cite is machine-resolved before a human verifies, distinguishing a real cite from a hallucinated one instead of only recording that a human said so.
missing_slate.why: The spec calls this 'the room that makes the platform sellable'; the resolver is built next door and left unwired, so the firm backstops AI hallucination with the same unaided human judgment the tool is meant to check.

missing_slate.item: Document production + export: Bates-stamped production volumes, a Concordance .dat/.opt load file the other side can load, and redaction — the review set can be coded but cannot be produced or exported.
missing_slate.why: The spec's core discovery deliverable is 'produce the volumes and load file the other side can actually load' and 'apply redactions'; without it the review work stays trapped inside Chambers.

missing_slate.item: Billing / invoice run: generate invoices from ledger fees + unbilled WIP, with write-downs and a fee-agreement-aware run (hourly/flat/contingency).
missing_slate.why: Flagged in prior review and still absent; the platform tracks time and trust but cannot turn recorded work into a bill, so revenue capture lives outside the tool.

missing_slate.item: Trust accounting By-Law 9 controls: three-way reconciliation, no-overdraw-per-matter enforcement, retainer replenishment triggers, and trust-transfer authorization records in Trust & Books.
missing_slate.why: Flagged in prior review; a Law Society trust account without By-Law 9 controls is a compliance and defalcation risk, and retainer signing (improve #6) needs a compliant trust side to post into.

missing_slate.item: Former-client, positional and imputed-conflict handling plus a real lateral-hire prior-firm screening workflow (the 'Lateral hire' role exists but does nothing).
missing_slate.why: Current-adverse token matching is only the easy third of the conflicts duty; former-client and imputed conflicts are where firms actually get disqualified, and the room claims to be the platform's rule-of-conduct anchor.

missing_slate.item: Notice-period and discoverability trap rules beyond the single basic limitation: Ontario Municipal Act s.44(10) 10-day notice, notice to the Crown, and limitation variants keyed to claim type.
missing_slate.why: Intake's spec promises 'limitation and notice periods including discoverability rules and municipal notice traps'; these short windows are where files die and none exist in the rules tranche or intake flow.

missing_slate.item: Chronology-driven downstream generation: a timeline/narrative export and a feed into Brief Writer's fact section and deposition outlines, so pleadings/briefs/exam outlines are generated from one sourced fact set.
missing_slate.why: The anti-drift promise — one sourced set of facts feeding every filing — is the room's reason to exist, but today the chronology is read-only in one direction.

missing_slate.item: Affidavit of documents with Schedule A/B/C (Ontario r.30.03), derived from Document Review coding — the Canadian analogue to the production list and privilege log.
missing_slate.why: A Toronto firm's sworn production instrument is absent while the US-style privilege log is present; it should generate from the same coding so it cannot drift.

missing_slate.item: Discovery plan / proportionality record (Ontario r.29.1, FRCP 26(f)), an interrogatory-count limiter (25-question cap), and a meet-and-confer / motion-to-compel log for FRCP 37(a)(1) certification.
missing_slate.why: In Ontario a discovery plan is mandatory and its absence is itself sanctionable, and the deficiency letter promises a meet-and-confer the file has nowhere to record.

missing_slate.item: Pleadings defence side: affirmative defences, counterclaims, and the waiver trap (defences waived if omitted); plus editable/jurisdictional element sets rather than a fixed 4-item menu.
missing_slate.why: Half of pleadings practice is defensive and 'affirmative defences waived if omitted' is a named malpractice trap the room advertises and does not deliver; a real matter's causes rarely all sit in a hardcoded four-item list.

missing_slate.item: Client portal: authenticated client-facing view of matter status updates, decision memos, budget-vs-actual and document delivery, with actual send/delivery of the Client Desk updates that are today only recorded.
missing_slate.why: Flagged in prior review; Client Desk is named for updates 'on a cadence instead of on request' but updates are never delivered and clients have no way to see their matter.

missing_slate.item: Expert disclosure instruments and independence tracking: Ontario Form 53 duty acknowledgment, FRCP 26(a)(2)(B) report-contents checklist, retention letters with rate bands by discipline, and prior-testimony/independence history.
missing_slate.why: Ontario reports are inadmissible without the signed Form 53, and Daubert/White Burgess challenges turn on prior exclusions and independence — none of it can be produced or tracked today.

selflearning_ideas: Citation verification reuse bank: once an authority is human-verified (resolves/pinpoint/quote/treatment) with the stored source excerpt and pinpoint text, cache it firm-wide keyed by normalized citation; when the same authority is cited in a later brief it pre-fills as 'previously verified on [date] by [name]' so the verifier confirms rather than re-reads from scratch. Purely a lookup cache of the firm's own attestations, not model retraining.

Conflicts alias/normalization dictionary: accumulate the party-name variants, corporate stop-word patterns and known aliases seen across past conflict runs into a firm alias table, so repeat opposing parties resolve faster and recurring false-positive tokens can be down-weighted with a recorded human reason.

Deadline/rule correction ledger: every time a lawyer overrides a computed deadline, capture the corrected date + reason; surface 'this rule has been overridden N times' next to the rule in rules.js so the firm's own practice corrects the reference data instead of silently diverging from it.

Boilerplate-objection corpus: store the objection language the firm and its opponents actually used plus how each resolved (withdrawn / motion / sanctioned), turning the single length<90 regex into a firm-labeled phrase list that flags padded boilerplate the regex misses.

Element-set and cause-of-action reuse bank: persist the custom causes, elements and jurisdictional variants lawyers add in Pleadings so they are reusable across matters by jurisdiction, growing the hardcoded menu from real filings.

Clause/template bank for retainers and letters: freeze the evergreen, contingency-disclosure, termination and cost-responsibility clause sets from accepted retainers as reusable, jurisdiction-tagged templates the next engagement letter is assembled from.

Plain-language substitution list from Client Desk: track which status-update phrases were flagged by the Gunning-fog scorer and how the lawyer rewrote them, building a firm phrase-swap dictionary that pre-suggests plainer wording on the next update.

Court/judge directory freshness from filing outcomes: when a filing to a court succeeds or is bounced, auto-refresh that court's verified-on date in the Court Book and attach the observed reason (page limit, judge individual rule) so directory staleness is driven by real filing history.

Case-value calibration from recorded judgments: compare Case Value's predicted settle-vs-try bands against actual outcomes captured in the Judgment room and report the firm's own realized-vs-predicted spread, so the liability/damage multipliers are tuned to this firm's results (descriptive statistics, not a trained model).

Expert reuse bank: track experts the firm has used with their rate history, disciplines, and prior qualification/exclusion outcomes, so the roster pre-fills and flags a repeat expert's prior exclusion when they are next proposed.

Chronology fact-to-name resolution memory: record the confirmed actor-name mappings a lawyer accepts when the deposition outline's fuzzy match asks (e.g. 'J. Doe' = 'Jane Doe'), and reuse them per matter so future outline pulls stop dropping or mis-attributing facts.
